title: Damit fing es an
subtitle: Science and the environment: cause, effect, and words that point back
words.intro: German researchers spend whole winters on a ship frozen into the Arctic ice, and come home to explain to their neighbours why the summer is hot. Science here is a public argument.

grammar[0].fact: German likes a thorough *Studie*, and it usually comes with a *Gegenstudie*. The Klimahaus in Bremerhaven lets you travel along one line of longitude through several climates, in one building, in a single afternoon.

grammar[1].blocks[0].note: An -r- before a vowel. At the start, the verb comes next: Damit kaufte er …

grammar[1].fact: German school essays are marked down for repeating a noun. So learners of German must master *dieser*, *jener*, *dadurch* and *damit* to get the marks. A good German paragraph hardly names its subject twice.

document.intro: A real sign in a field, on the fence of a weather station. In three calm sentences, it tells you what science does with the weather: passive voice, folded phrases, and one polite request.
document.fact: The *Deutscher Wetterdienst* has its head office in Offenbach, and its data comes from stations like this one.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Join each pair with dadurch, damit or dafür.

document.tasks[1].items[0].answer: Die Station misst das Wetter. Dadurch wird die Vorhersage besser.
reading.intro: Lena’s cousin has come home from a research ship. She is Dr. Anne Rainer, and she has spent a year measuring Arctic ice. She has been asked to give a talk in the village hall. It has gone well until the questions. Frau Huber, who is visiting, has her hand up.
reading.fact: Germany’s research ship *Polarstern* drifted frozen in the Arctic ice for a year in 2019 and 2020, on the largest polar expedition ever. Armed polar bear watches stood guard while the scientists worked on the ice.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Complete with damit, dadurch, darauf or daran.
